note: Bortle values are approximate classes for the general area, not measurements. Verify any site on lightpollutionmap.info before travelling.

sites.name: Bhandardara
sites.note: Lake and hill area in the Sahyadris with open ridges around Arthur Lake. Expect some light domes on the horizon from nearby towns.

sites.name: Kaas Plateau
sites.note: Open high plateau with wide horizons. It is a protected seasonal flower reserve, so check entry rules before planning a night visit.

sites.name: Tamhini Ghat
sites.note: Forested ghat road with limited open ground. Scout a clear pull-off in daylight.

sites.name: Pawna Lake
sites.note: Popular lakeside camping close to Pune. Easy access, but expect more skyglow than the deeper Sahyadri sites.

sites.name: Malshej Ghat
sites.note: High ghat with open viewpoints. The monsoon is cloudy, so plan for roughly October to April.

sites.name: Bhimashankar
sites.note: Forest sanctuary and temple town. Check sanctuary timings and observe from open areas outside the forest.

sites.name: Rann of Kutch (Dhordo)
sites.note: Flat white salt desert with a huge open horizon. Best in the cool season. Check permit requirements and festival dates.

sites.name: Sam Sand Dunes
sites.note: Desert dunes west of Jaisalmer. Tourist camps can be bright, so walk out beyond the camp lights.

sites.name: Kibber, Spiti
sites.note: One of the highest villages reachable by road. Excellent skies in the cold season. Plan for altitude and possible road closures.

sites.name: Hanle Dark Sky Reserve
sites.note: India's first dark sky reserve, home to the Indian Astronomical Observatory. Check permit requirements and acclimatise before going.

sites.name: Pangong Tso
sites.note: High-altitude lake with very dark skies away from camps. Check permit requirements and altitude advice.

sites.name: Mauna Kea Visitor Area
sites.note: Stargazing at the visitor area on the mountain. Summit access has restrictions, so check current rules.

sites.name: San Pedro de Atacama
sites.note: Dry high desert with some of the clearest skies on Earth. Town lights are bright, so move out into the desert.

sites.name: Cherry Springs State Park
sites.note: Designated dark sky park with a dedicated observing field. Check seasonal rules.

sites.name: NamibRand Nature Reserve
sites.note: International Dark Sky Reserve in the Namib Desert. Check access and booking rules before travelling.

sites.name: Lake Tekapo
sites.note: Core of the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve. The town uses controlled lighting.

sites.name: Roque de los Muchachos
sites.note: Observatory ridge with exceptionally dark skies. Check road and access rules.
